title: Audit Plan Manifest
description: Schema for the audit orchestrator manifest (default docs/audit/audit-plan.json). All fields new in the plugin version are OPTIONAL so a pre-existing manifest validates unchanged after adding "$schema". additionalProperties is permissive at object levels to stay back-compatible; enums are enforced on the orchestrator-controlled fields (task/phase status, tests.mode, task.risk) to catch typos, while human-authored review fields (review.status, finding.severity) stay free-text.

fileIndex.description: Map of repo-relative file path -> array of task ids that touch it. Used for phase review scope and parallelization hints.

bugs.description: Optional bug tracker. Bugs live outside phases (a reported bug is not yet a plan); /audit:bug fix materializes a bug into a tdd task in a bugfix phase, linked via bug.taskId <-> task.bugId.

status.description: Lifecycle state for a phase or task. Two of the five are TERMINAL: 'done' (the work landed) and 'cancelled' (the work will not be done - the feature was dropped, the approach was abandoned, the phase closes with whatever landed). Cancelled is the phase/task twin of a bug's 'wontfix', and the state the trackers call Canceled (Linear), Won't Do (Jira), closed-as-not-planned (GitHub) and Removed (Azure DevOps). Nothing is deleted to express it: a cancelled item keeps its history, its commits and its outcome, and the report files it under the archive beside the done ones. Readiness treats a cancelled blocker as settled - a plan must not deadlock on work nobody will do - so a task waiting on a cancelled one becomes ready and is worth a look before it runs.

model.description: Model tier the orchestrator spawns. Names are illustrative; adapt to your provider.

meta.description: Global configuration. version is the only strictly required field.

version.description: Manifest schema version. 2 = single-file layout; 3 = sharded layout (this file is the index; each phase body lives in phases/<id>.json). Readers accept both via _manifest_io.

developmentBranch.description: Parent branch audit branches fork from and ff-merge back into. Default 'main' when omitted.

branchPrefix.description: Prefix for per-phase branches, e.g. 'audit' -> audit/<phaseId>-<slug>. Default 'audit'. SUPERSEDED by meta.branch, which is read first; this key stays valid and keeps working so existing manifests are unaffected. When both are present meta.branch wins and /audit:doctor says which shape produced the name.

branch.description: Branch-naming convention. Absent => the meta.branchPrefix shape, i.e. '{branchPrefix}/{phase}-{slug}' with the default prefix 'audit'. A template rather than a set of flags, so a team expresses its own convention without the plugin growing a setting per variation.

template.description: Branch name template. Placeholders: {type} {initials} {phase} {slug}. Example '{type}/{initials}/{phase}-{slug}' -> feature/jd/p2-chart-export. A placeholder that resolves to nothing collapses together with the separator that follows it, so an absent {initials} yields feature/p2-chart-export and never feature//p2-chart-export. The result must be a legal git ref; validate-manifest.py rejects one that is not.

defaultType.description: The {type} used when a phase neither sets branchType nor derives one. Default 'feature'.

types.description: The types phase.branchType may name. Default: feature, bugfix, hotfix, release, docs, refactor, test, chore. This list is ALSO what the orchestrator's pre-approved branch globs are derived from (reference/orchestrator.md -> Branch operations), so a type missing here means a permission prompt on every branch operation that uses it.

initials.description: Value for {initials}. null/absent => derive from the git identity the usage ledger already resolves (git user.name -> initials). Set it explicitly when the git name does not initial usefully. Not an identity of record: the audit trail's author is the usage ledger's, not this.

slugMaxLength.description: Cap on the {slug} segment derived from phase.title. Default 30.

gitRoot.description: Path (relative to the project directory) of the git repository root, where all git operations and build/gate commands run. Default '.' (the project directory IS the git root — the normal case). Set to e.g. 'test' when the git repo / workspace lives in a subdirectory; the orchestrator then runs `git -C <gitRoot>` and strips the prefix when staging. Keep it in sync with the hooks' `gitRoot` in .claude/audit.config.json.

reviewSkill.description: Skill invoked at phase sign-off. null (default) => skip review; tests are the signer. A phase may override it (phase.reviewSkill), and a registered area may sit between the two — resolved phase.reviewSkill ?? meta.areas[tag].reviewSkill ?? meta.reviewSkill.

areas.description: Registry of the areas a phase's `area` tag can name — the monorepo half of the plugin. Optional in both directions and back-compatible by construction: a tag with no entry here stays legal (the validator warns; nothing refuses), and an entry no phase uses is legal too. Registering a tag is what gives it properties: a root directory, a description, a default sign-off reviewer, default executor skills and an advisory owner. Resolution is phase.reviewSkill ?? areas[tag].reviewSkill ?? meta.reviewSkill for the reviewer, and area skills + task.skills (deduped, area first) for the executor. When a phase carries several tags, WRITTEN ORDER decides — the first tag whose area declares the field answers.

reportSummary.description: Optional plain-language narrative shown in a Summary box atop the rendered report (render-report.py). /audit:report usually supplies this via --summary-file (read-only) rather than storing it here.

reportBasename.description: Optional basename for the generated report files, e.g. 'q3-audit' => q3-audit.html/.md (default 'audit-report'). Sanitized to [A-Za-z0-9-_]; overridable per-run with render-report.py --basename.

runtimeBoot.description: Optional runtime smoke gate. null (default) => skipped.

appRootPath.description: Source root; boot gate applies when a phase touches it.

nodePreamble.description: Shell prefix run (un-piped) before build gates, e.g. 'source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use'. null => run gates directly.

coauthor.description: Trailer appended to commit messages, or null.

buildCommands.description: Optional template map so gate entries like 'test:<project>' resolve to a real command instead of hardcoding a build tool. Keys are free (lint/test/typecheck/...).

ado.description: Azure DevOps sync configuration for /audit:sync. null/absent => sync refuses with setup guidance. Never store credentials here — auth belongs to `az login` / AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT.

types.description: Work-item type mapping. Defaults: bug -> 'Bug', task -> 'Task', pbi -> auto-detect.

pbi.description: Phase-level work item type, used when phaseWorkItems is true. null/absent = auto-detect at the first phase push (Product Backlog Item > User Story > Requirement > Issue, whichever the project's process defines) and write the pick back here under /audit:sync's confirm gate — so it is deterministic after the first run and visible in the file.

identityMap.description: Advisory map from a LEDGER identity to that person's ADO identity (email/UPN). Each key is written in the SAME form usage.authorMode records authors and area.owner is written in (git user.email under the default 'email' mode, user.name under 'name') — the ledger identity is the key because it is the identity the plugin already owns (the usage ledger's author column, area owners). /audit:sync reads it in both directions: push PROPOSES --assigned-to for the mapped owner of an item's area (it asks first and never assigns silently); pull reverse-maps a mapped ADO assignee into reportedBy's ledger form (unmapped assignees keep the 'ado:' prefix). Advisory only: nothing gates, refuses or assigns on this map by itself, and absent/null means 'no mapping' — sync simply stops proposing.

enabled.description: Master switch for the connector. Absent = on (an existing meta.ado keeps working unchanged). false stops /audit:sync push and pull and the orchestration echo; links already written are kept, and /audit:sync status still runs, reporting the linked items as frozen. Set true or remove the key to turn back on.

tag.description: The provenance tag stamped on every pushed/echoed work item. Absent = 'audit-plugin'; a custom value (e.g. a per-repo tag) pairs naturally with pull.tags so a shared sprint's push and pull are symmetric per repo; explicit null = no tag at all. Tag writes always READ-MERGE-WRITE the item's tag list (System.Tags updates are wholesale — writing blind would erase the team's own tags). The `blocked` marker is separate and fixed: a state signal, not branding.

parentWorkItem.description: The EXISTING Azure DevOps work item that audit work hangs under — typically a Feature or Epic already on the team's backlog. Absent/null = the connector builds its own branch (phaseWorkItems creates a phase item with nothing above it), which is correct and puts audit work BESIDE the team's planning instead of inside it: nobody planning from that board sees it. Set it and created phase items become children of that id (and, with phaseWorkItems false, tasks do). An id and therefore an integer — a config carrying "103205" as a string is a typo worth naming rather than coercing, because coercing hides it.

conventions.description: What a work item must look like to BELONG on this board. A property of the BOARD, not of the plugin: absent/null means the board has no standard and every item conforms trivially — not 'could not check', but 'there is nothing to check'. Graded by scripts/manifest/_ado_conventions.py, which is also what the writing side runs an item through before creating it, so the rule is executed rather than remembered. Without this, the connector writes work items that are mechanically correct and visibly foreign on a governed board: no description skeleton, no mandatory 'Done when', tags outside the agreed vocabulary, and a hierarchy the connector built for itself beside the team's backlog instead of inside it.

requiredFields.description: {work item type: [ADO field reference name, ...]} — fields that must be present and non-empty. Scoped BY TYPE because a story and a task do not owe the same fields; a checker that demanded acceptance criteria on a task would be switched off.

descriptionMustContain.description: {work item type: [literal marker, ...]} — how a description skeleton is enforced. Matching is case-insensitive, so 'DONE WHEN:' is the same skeleton as 'Done when:'.

tagVocabulary.description: {tag prefix: [allowed value, ...]} for tags shaped `prefix:value`. The key "*" is the explicit opt-in for bare, unprefixed tags — spelled rather than implied, so a board that forbids free-form tags gets a finding on the first one instead of silently accepting anything without a colon. An EMPTY object forbids every tag and is warned about, since that is almost never meant.

requireParent.description: true = every pushed item must hang under a parent work item. For a team that already has a Feature/Story backlog this is what puts audit work INSIDE their planning rather than beside it.

echo.description: Orchestration echo switch. Absent = ON: when a linked task goes done or blocked (or a done task is reopened via /audit:run) and at phase sign-off, the orchestrator best-effort UPDATES the already-linked work item — state per stateMap, Remaining Work per onComplete, comments per comments. The echo never creates work items and never asks questions; creation happens only in /audit:sync push behind its confirm gate, and a failed echo is one report line healed by the next /audit:sync push. false = manual-only sync.

phaseWorkItems.description: Absent = ON: /audit:sync push creates one types.pbi work item per phase and parent-links each of the phase's task/bug work items under it (System.LinkTypes.Hierarchy), writing phase.ado. The push plan lists the PBI creates and is confirm-gated, so nothing appears in ADO unseen. false = flat push, no phase-level items.

stateMap.description: Manifest status -> ADO state name, per item kind. Absent/null = the built-in defaults (task: pending>New, in_progress>Active, blocked>Active+tag, done>Closed; bug: open>New, triaged/in_progress>Active, fixed>Resolved, wontfix>Closed; phase: the task defaults). A key set to null means 'never move state for this transition' — the team moves that card by hand. NOTE the built-in defaults name Agile-process states; Scrum tasks use To Do/In Progress/Done, so Scrum projects should set this map. The `phase` block exists because phase work items (PBI/User Story) carry a DIFFERENT state vocabulary than tasks — a Scrum PBI knows New/Approved/Committed/Done and no 'In Progress'. States are applied by UPDATE after create (ADO allows only the initial state at creation), and a state the process rejects degrades per item. Cards move via System.State only — a board column not backed by a state is unreachable, and sync says so rather than faking it.

onComplete.description: What a task's done-transition writes besides state. Absent/null = touch nothing.

remainingWork.description: Written to Microsoft.VSTS.Scheduling.RemainingWork in the same update as the done move (task-category types only — PBIs do not carry the field in most processes). Default when onComplete is present without this key: 0. Explicit null = never touch the field.

comments.description: Generated work-item comments. Absent/null = none. (The legacy 'Fixed in <sha>' comment on a bug closed with fixedIn is part of the field mapping and unaffected by this key.)

onBlocked.description: Default false. When a linked task goes blocked, comment with attempts, the last outcome and the blockers digest.

onComplete.description: Default false. On the done move, comment with the sign-off note and the task's commit sha.

sprint.description: Dynamic iteration resolution. Absent/null = the static meta.ado.iterationPath (or no stamp). When set, /audit:sync resolves the team's CURRENT iteration at push time, stamps System.IterationPath on created/updated items and records phase.ado.iterationPath; a failed resolution falls back to iterationPath with one warning and never aborts the run.

team.description: The ADO team whose iteration calendar defines 'current'.

mode.description: Only 'current' today; the enum leaves room.

pull.description: Scoping filters for sprint pull — one sprint can span multiple repos, and these say which items belong to THIS repo's manifest. Filters AND-compose; either alone suffices. With NO filter configured, pull refuses to import blind: it lists the sprint's items, requires explicit selection, and offers to persist the chosen filter here. Regardless of filters, pull always confirms the candidate list before writing proposals.

areaPath.description: WIQL 'UNDER' filter for sprint pull. Absent/null = fall back to meta.ado.areaPath.

tags.description: System.Tags CONTAINS filters, e.g. a per-repo tag.

usage.description: Where the report/panel/status commands read token-usage data from. The hooks read their own copy from .claude/audit.config.json - that split (commands from manifest meta, hooks from the config file) is the plugin's standing convention. Both default to '.claude/usage', so the two only need to agree when a project moves the ledger.

ledgerDir.description: Repo-relative directory holding the monthly NDJSON usage ledger. Default '.claude/usage'. Must match usage.ledgerDir in .claude/audit.config.json when either is customized.

showCost.description: Render equivalent API cost alongside token counts. Default true.

pricingAsOf.description: Date the pricing table behind the stored costs was accurate, surfaced in the report so a stale rate is visible rather than silent.

area.description: One registered area (an app, service, package or cross-cutting concern) that a phase's `area` tag can name.

root.description: Directory this area lives in, relative to the PROJECT directory — the same origin as task.files and the fileIndex keys, so it carries the meta.gitRoot prefix when the workspace is in a subdirectory. /audit:doctor warns when it is not a directory; an absolute path warns because it cannot resolve in a second clone.

description.description: One line saying what this area is, for the humans reading status/report/panel.

reviewSkill.description: Default sign-off reviewer for phases tagged with this area, between phase.reviewSkill (wins) and meta.reviewSkill (fallback). Explicit null means 'tests are the signer here' and STOPS the fallback — it is an answer, not a miss.

skills.description: Skills every executor subagent working in this area loads BEFORE the task's own — house conventions first, task specifics second. Merged with task.skills and deduped, area first. Explicit null is allowed for symmetry with task.skills and is EQUIVALENT to []: the area is itself the fallback, so there is nothing beneath it for a null to stop — it reads as 'this area deliberately declares no defaults', and resolution treats both as contributing nothing.

owner.description: Who to coordinate with about this area, written in the SAME form usage.authorMode records authors (git user.email under the default 'email' mode, user.name under 'name') so the ledger's author column and this field are one identity. Advisory only: nothing gates, refuses or assigns on it — the plan-gate hook adds a heads-up note when someone else edits here, and status/panel display it. Explicit null is an answer ('nobody owns this') and stops the written-order lookup, exactly like reviewSkill.

adoLink.description: Azure DevOps work-item link, written by /audit:sync after a successful push (never by hand). Additive — absent until the first sync.

id.description: Work-item id in the configured project.

url.description: Web link to the work item.

lastSyncedAt.description: ISO timestamp of the last successful sync of this item.

iterationPath.description: The iteration this item was last stamped into by /audit:sync (sprint mode 'current'). Recorded so status can report sprint drift after a rollover. Absent until a sprint-mode push.

origin.description: Where this work item came from: 'created' = /audit:sync push created it, 'imported' = pull adopted a card somebody else made. ABSENT/null = unrecorded (a link written before this field existed, or by hand) and every surface says so rather than assuming 'created' — putting this plugin's name on somebody else's card is the one wrong answer available here. Two values because only two code paths write one; the provenance tag cannot answer this question, since meta.ado.tag is merged onto every item a push TOUCHES. Read by /audit:sync (the push plan says whether it is about to write to a card it did not create) and by /audit:doctor's 'ado links' row.

phase.description: A phase. In the single-file layout it carries its full body (status + tasks + ...). In the v3 SHARDED layout the top-level phases[] holds lightweight STUBS ({id, title, shard}) that point at phases/<id>.json, where the full body lives; only id/title are required here because a stub omits status/tasks. The referential validator (validate-manifest.py) runs on the ASSEMBLED manifest and enforces that every phase ultimately has a status and tasks.

shard.description: v3 sharded layout: relative path (from the index) to this phase's shard file, e.g. 'phases/P2.json'. Present only on an index stub.

priority.description: Which phase the orchestrator reaches for first among the tasks that are ALREADY ready. It never makes an unready task ready and never skips a dependency: a pinned phase whose blockedBy is unsatisfied is skipped, and /audit:status says so. Tier 1 is unique (a second holder is a warning naming the manifest-order tie-break); higher tiers are shared. An ABSENT priority means unprioritised — it sorts after every prioritised phase and keeps manifest order among its peers, so a plan with no priority anywhere runs exactly as it did before the field existed. INDEX-ONLY in the v3 sharded layout: it belongs on the index stub, which already carries status, so execution order is computable without opening a shard; a copy found in a shard body is ignored and reported.

budgetUSD.description: Spend ceiling for this phase in USD. Compared against the token ledger by /audit:usage, /audit:status and the report, and gateable via `audit-status.py --fail-on over-budget|budget-80`. A value of 0 or below is not a budget of zero — it is rejected, because an unbudgeted phase must render as 'no budget' rather than as infinitely over.

blockedBy.description: Phase ids that must be done before this phase's tasks are ready.

description.description: Optional prose description of the phase (free text; informational).

desiredOutcome.description: One-line statement of what success looks like for the phase. Shown by /audit:status, given to every task subagent, and phase.summary must address it at sign-off.

testGate.description: Commands (or 'key:project' entries resolved via meta.buildCommands) that must all pass at sign-off.

parentBranch.description: Branch THIS phase forks from and merges back into, overriding meta.developmentBranch (the default/fallback). Lets a phase integrate into a story branch, a release line, or another phase's branch instead of the repo's development branch. null/absent => use meta.developmentBranch. Resolution is the same chain reviewSkill uses. A phase whose parent is not meta.developmentBranch has NOT reached the development branch when it signs off, and the sign-off report says so.

branchType.description: The {type} segment of this phase's branch name, overriding the derived default. Must be one of meta.branch.types. null/absent => derive: a phase materialized from a bugs[] entry gives 'bugfix', anything else meta.branch.defaultType.

baseRef.description: HEAD SHA at phase start; set by the orchestrator. Records WHICH COMMIT the phase started from; parentBranch records which branch that commit came from.

branch.description: Local phase branch; set at phase start.

mergedAt.description: ISO timestamp after ff-merge to the development branch.

ado.description: Azure DevOps link for this phase's work item (created when meta.ado.phaseWorkItems is true). Written only by /audit:sync, like every adoLink.

reviewSkill.description: Skill invoked at THIS phase's sign-off, overriding meta.reviewSkill (which is the default/fallback). Lets a monorepo review backend vs mobile vs web phases with different reviewers. null/absent => use meta.reviewSkill.

area.description: App/domain/concern label(s) for grouping & filtering phases in status/report/panel. A single string (a partition, e.g. 'backend') OR a list of tags for cross-cutting concerns (e.g. ['backend', 'security'] — the phase is grouped under EACH; written order decides which area answers when several could). Any vocabulary: backend/mobile/web, devops, security, embedded, data, ml, platform… Free text stays legal. A tag that also has an entry in meta.areas gains that area's root, default reviewSkill and default executor skills; an unregistered tag is informational only, and the validator warns about it ONLY when the manifest registers areas at all (where it is usually a typo).

reviewFindings.description: Legacy (pre-plugin manifests) running tally of sign-off findings — informational only; the orchestrator does not read it.

skills.description: Skills the executor subagent loads (via the Skill tool) before writing code for this task. The area's skills load first, then these, deduped — so a house convention cannot be displaced by a task-specific one. Explicit null means 'no skills apply to this task' and STOPS the area fallback — nothing loads even when the area declares defaults; it is an answer, not a miss, exactly like reviewSkill. [] or absent means unconsidered: the area default still applies.

blockedBy.description: HARD GATE (cross-phase or cross-task): task/phase ids that must be done before this task is READY. Use for phase boundaries and prerequisites.

dependsOn.description: INTRA-PHASE ORDERING & PARALLELIZATION: task ids that must be done first. Tasks with disjoint `files` AND satisfied `dependsOn` may run in parallel. (blockedBy = when a task may START; dependsOn = ordering among startable siblings.)

files.description: Repo-relative files this task touches (optional :line-range suffix). Union across a phase = its review scope.

commit.description: SHA of the per-task commit; null until committed.

attempts.description: Times this task has been spawned; incremented per execution.

maxAttempts.description: Stop retrying and mark 'blocked' once attempts reaches this (default 3).

risk.description: low = mechanical; med = behavior change; high = irreversible/auth/migration (never haiku, human-confirm before commit). null for historical tasks.

verifiedBy.description: Test names/ids this task added, linking code to its guard.

bugId.description: Link to bugs[].id when this task was materialized via /audit:bug fix. The orchestrator flips that bug to 'fixed' (+fixedIn) when the task commits.

movedFrom.description: Written by /audit:task move when a task is renumbered into another phase: the id and phase it held before, and when it moved. The journal's chained task.move row is the other half of the mapping; historical ledger rows keep the OLD taskId, and this field is what lets a reader join them.

phase.description: The phase it lived in before the move.

bugStatus.description: Bug lifecycle. in_progress = materialized into a task; fixed = that task committed.

claim.description: v3 optimistic parallel-run claim: which session/host/branch is running this phase. Lives in the phase shard body so a same-phase double-claim across branches shows up as a shard merge conflict. Optional; released (removed) when the phase finishes.

at.description: ISO timestamp the claim was taken.

repro.description: Reproduction steps: a string or array of step strings.

taskId.description: Task materialized for this bug via /audit:bug fix; null until then.

fixedIn.description: Commit SHA of the fixing task; written by the audit orchestrator.

mode.description: tdd = write a failing test first (proves the bug), then fix. regression = fix, then add a locking test. gate-only = no new test; keep existing gates green.

add.description: Assertions/tests to author. For mode 'tdd' these describe tests that MUST FAIL on current code (discover-then-fix). For mode 'regression' they describe the guard(s) added AFTER the fix. The meaning is mode-dependent — see `expectRedFirst`.

expectRedFirst.description: Machine-readable disambiguation of `add`: true (typical for tdd) means the tests are expected to fail on current code before the fix.

gate.description: Commands (or 'key:project' entries resolved via meta.buildCommands) that must pass.

outcome.description: Written by the ORCHESTRATOR (not the subagent) on completion. Overwritten on re-run.

technical.description: What was actually done (changes, commands, test counts).

status.description: Free-text in practice (e.g. 'pending', 'passed', 'skipped', or a descriptive note). Not enum-constrained for back-compat.

findings.description: Each finding is a structured object (preferred) or a plain string (legacy).

severity.description: Free-text in practice (low/med/high/medium/LOW/info/...). Not enum-constrained for back-compat.

items.description: Each item is a structured object (preferred) or a plain string (legacy).

id.description: PROP-<n>, allocated repo-wide like BUG-<n>. Legacy free-form ids are tolerated (validator warns, never fails).

status.description: proposed | materialized | dropped (validator-enforced vocabulary for payload-bearing proposals).

createdISO.description: ISO timestamp when the proposal was parked.

payload.description: The full synthesized phase, parked losslessly so materialization is a move, not a re-synthesis. The phase id inside is RESERVED: id allocation counts it alongside live phases. fileIndex is deliberately not stored here — it is derived from payload.phase.tasks[].files at materialize time.

materializedAs.description: Phase id this proposal became, written by /audit:propose materialize (never by hand).

notes.description: Why a proposal was declined - REQUIRED once status is 'dropped'. /audit:propose drop asks for it when not given, because a dropped proposal is history rather than a deletion and a later reader must find why the work was declined. Was tolerated off-schema for as long as only that command wrote it; it is declared here now that the panel can drop too.

droppedAt.description: ISO timestamp of the drop, the counterpart of materializedAt. Set only when status is 'dropped'.
